name: Growing
label: Kranky
lede: A bassist and a left-handed guitarist from Olympia who built cathedral-sized drones out of volume pedals, got louder, moved to Brooklyn, found a beat, and never once stopped between songs to talk.

eras.title: Olympia, and a lot of volume pedals
eras.text: Growing started as a trio in Olympia, Washington, and quickly shrank to Kevin Doria on bass and Joe Denardo on guitar. Two long, slow, enormous records for Kranky put them next to Stars of the Lid and Labradford, only louder.

q: basically, our whole band is volume pedals.
years.h: Kevin Doria, Joe Denardo and Zack Carlson start Growing in Olympia
years.p: A bass, a guitar and drums. The songs are slow instrumental drones, built from delay and looper pedals, feedback, EBow and phrase samplers run through parallel amps.
years.xp: Denardo is left-handed and Doria right-handed, so on stage they mirror each other. Both run effects chains into several amps at once for a stereo spread.

years.h: The Sky's Run into the Sea · Kranky
years.p: Growing's first album, on CD and LP: long instrumental pieces that often pass ten minutes.

years.h: Zack Carlson leaves; Growing becomes a duo
years.p: The drummer departs after the first album. Doria and Denardo carry on as a two-piece until 2009.

years.h: The Soul of the Rainbow and the Harmony of Light · the second Kranky record
years.p: Co-released with Animal Disguise. Early versions circulated as the Early Stages CD-R bootleg.

eras.title: Brooklyn, and a pulse
eras.text: Growing moved to Brooklyn and away from Kranky, releasing on Megablade, Troubleman and The Social Registry. The ten-minute drones got shorter and started to push forward, and the band went to Europe with Boris.

years.p: The first of three Growing albums for Megablade. Conspiracy Records also puts out Live on CD and double LP.
Doria's side project releases a first album on Animal Disguise limited to 150 copies; a 500-copy vinyl follows in 2007.
The second Megablade album, as the drones start to shorten.
Released jointly with Troubleman Unlimited. Late that year Growing starts with The Social Registry on a 7-inch in its Social Club series.

years.h: Growing tours Europe and the UK with Boris
years.p: Doria and Denardo spend April on the road with the Japanese heavy band [[Boris|57652bf8-cfe8-42e7-b9a7-5572a7080d8d]].
After the mini-album Lateral, a full album that swaps ten-minute pieces for tracks of three to seven minutes.

eras.title: A third member and a Vice deal
eras.text: Sadie Laska of the Brooklyn noise duo IUD joined with samplers and a microphone, and Growing signed to Vice Records. The drone band now had rhythm, a singer's mic and a single.

years.h: Sadie Laska joins on samplers and microphone
years.p: Growing becomes a trio again for the first time since 2003.
The first album with Sadie Laska is rhythm-driven and short-form. The Village Voice covers the single Camera '84, the record and the new member.

years.h: Growing plays ATP, picked by Godspeed You! Black Emperor
years.p: [[Godspeed You! Black Emperor|3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4]] choose Growing for the All Tomorrow's Parties weekend they curate in December 2010.

eras.title: Back to two
eras.text: Doria and Denardo, now the whole band again, kept making records on their own schedule from Brooklyn.

years.p: The duo's latest album, two decades after Olympia.
